fg.note: The theme's own foreground. Every derived tone on the plate is mixed from this, never from rgba(255,255,255,...).

plate.note: The plate is the editor's own ground, separated by a scored border rather than a fill. editorWidget-background was measured and rejected: on Solarized Light it drops the theme's foreground pairing to 4.4:1.

plate-2.note: Key faces and the diagnostics latch only. Never behind small text.

well.note: Tape well, counter aperture, fader slot.

muted.note: Identical to fg by measurement, not by oversight. Kept as a name meaning 'this is a label, not a value'.

score.note: The only division device on the surface. Becomes var(--vscode-contrastBorder) in high contrast.

bevel.note: The single highlight in the system: 1px inset along the plate's top edge. Transparent in high contrast.

lamp.note: The lamp is the foreground, not the accent: lit key faces are the largest areas on the plate and an accent lamp outshouted the buffer signal.

accent.note: Spent only on the playhead, the decoded chunk register, its swatch, and the event-log source name.

focus.note: 2px ring at 2px offset. The locator model is keyboard-first.

ok-text.note: Signal hues pulled toward the foreground for anything read as text; the raw hues are for lamps and rails only.

warn-text.note: Chart yellow on a light plate measures under 3:1, and the underrun count must stay legible when it is the only thing wrong.

wave-past.note: The tape is ink and the buffer is accent; the two never share a hue, or the tape's coloured extent reads as the buffered extent.

wave-ghost.note: A constant low band where no envelope has been measured yet. 34% in high contrast.

mark-wash.note: Locators are told apart by form — bracket flags in the foreground — not by hue.

counter.purpose: The elapsed time: the largest object on the plate, 66px tabular mono in a milled aperture. Millisecond digits at 0.55em, baseline-dropped. 46px at 720px of container, 38px at 520px.

nameplate.purpose: The source name, inline beside its engraved legend and ellipsised. A nameplate, never a stacked header.

body.purpose: The dead-well hint at 46ch — the only running prose on the surface.

value.purpose: Every reported number and the error message: locators, total duration, data-line fields.

data.purpose: Diagnostics grids and the event log.

engraved.purpose: Every field label, key label, status word, bay head and secondary key. Tracking runs 0.10em on keys, 0.11em on the status word, 0.13em on field legends, 0.16em on the well title.

shadows.name: plate-bevel
shadows.purpose: The plate's own top edge. The only highlight in the system; transparent in high contrast.

shadows.name: recess-deep
shadows.purpose: The counter aperture — the deepest cut on the surface.

shadows.name: recess-shallow-channel
shadows.purpose: The key channel under the transport keys.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Background, border-color and color on keys, secondary keys and the diagnostics latch.

motion.name: flag
motion.purpose: The hover time flag over the tape well.

motion.name: lamp-pulse
motion.purpose: The status lamp while the machine is busy; opacity 1 to 0.3.

motion.name: scan
motion.purpose: Indeterminate progress while the index is read: a 34%-wide accent block sweeping a 120x2px bar. Present only in data-state=loading.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every animation and transition is neutralised, universally.

breakpoints.name: split
breakpoints.note: Container query on .cp-root, not a media query. Counter to 46px, keys to 46/54px, fader to 84px, well clamp(132px, 34vh, 320px).

breakpoints.name: panel
breakpoints.note: Container query. Bridge stacks: counter and level on row one, keys full width on row two at space-between. Buffer swatch key drops; locator readout stays.

canvasRegisters.name: ruler
canvasRegisters.note: Three-level tick hierarchy, 500 10px mono labels, tick steps 0.1s to 3600s.

canvasRegisters.name: tape
canvasRegisters.note: The field is a measurement, not a decoration.

canvasRegisters.name: chunk register
canvasRegisters.note: Accent decoded, amber in-flight, 15% unread; unread drawn as a 3px half-height band.

highContrast.note: Every derived tint collapses to the plain background, score and score-2 become var(--vscode-contrastBorder), bevel and lamp-bed go transparent, tape/tick/rail tints rise, guide and tick-major go to full foreground, and a lit key inverts (foreground face, background glyph) instead of picking up a 16% wash.

contrastMeasurements.note: Six theme fixtures in docs/design/player/. The 4.5 is Solarized Light's 66px counter, where the large-text floor is 3:1; every element at 12px or below clears 4.5:1 in all six. descriptionForeground against this plate measures 3.4:1 on Dracula and 3.6:1 on Solarized Light, which is why the plate uses one ink.

narrative.overview:
The surface is one machined plate, not a stack of cards. Everything sits on a single ground that is the editor's own background; the plate is separated from the editor by a scored border rather than by a fill, and its internal rows are separated by 1px scored hairlines that run edge to edge. Where the category ships a rounded card with a centred circular play button, this ships a bridge: engraved micro-caps legends, square keys that light along their bottom edge, a time counter set into a milled aperture at display scale, and a level fader running in a scored slot.

The palette is not ours and never will be. Every colour resolves from a --vscode-* token, so the plate adopts whatever theme is active — including high-contrast light and dark, which are a real code branch rather than a hope. Identity is therefore carried by four things only: geometry (2px corners, squares, no pills, no circles), density (10–16px padding, hairline divisions, no decorative whitespace), engraving (10px tracked caps as field labels) and lamp state (one lit key at a time). Derived tones are mixed against the theme's own foreground rather than layered as rgba(255,255,255,…), because a white overlay vanishes in a light theme.

Contrast headroom is treated as a budget the theme owns, not one we may spend. The plate adds no tonal step behind small text; the label/value hierarchy is a size-and-form step instead. Measured worst case across six theme fixtures: 8.6 / 9.8 / 21.0 / 10.5 / 4.5 / 10.8, where the 4.5 is Solarized Light's 66px counter and the large-text floor is 3:1. Every element at 12px or below clears 4.5:1 in all six.
keyCharacteristics: One plate; rows divided by scored 1px hairlines, never by gaps between boxes.
2px milled corners everywhere; no pill, no circle, no capsule.
Recesses, not raised cards: depth is inset shadow plus a scored border.
Engraved 10px tracked caps for every field label; monospace for every value.
One lamp at a time; the lamp is the foreground, not the accent.
The accent belongs to the stream (playhead, chunk register) and nothing else.
Layout responds to the container, not the viewport.

rules.name: The Guest Palette Rule
rules.body: Every colour resolves from a --vscode-* token. Hex appears only as a var() fallback for the standalone demo and is never a design value. No owned accent, ever.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: The plate has exactly one text colour. Solarized Light pairs its own foreground with its own background at 4.78:1, so there is no headroom for a tonal step: even a 6% step put 10px labels under 4.5:1. Hierarchy comes from size, tracking, weight and scale instead.

rules.name: The Nothing-Tints-Behind-Text Rule
rules.body: No surface behind small text carries a derived tint. A 10% error tint on the status band measured 4.34:1 on Solarized Light, so the error state is scored in the error hue (1px top and bottom at 60%) rather than filled with it.

rules.name: The Accent Belongs to the Stream Rule
rules.body: The accent marks decoded-right-now and the playhead. The tape is ink and the lamp is foreground, precisely so the coloured extent of the tape can never be misread as the buffered extent.

rules.name: The High-Contrast Branch Rule
rules.body: Under body.vscode-high-contrast / .vscode-high-contrast-light, every derived tint collapses to the plain background, every score becomes contrastBorder, bevel and lamp-bed go transparent, and a lit key inverts (foreground face, background glyph). A 16% wash is invisible on those grounds.

rules.name: The Size-Step Rule
rules.body: The label/value hierarchy is a size and form step, not a tone step: 10px tracked caps against 11.5px tabular mono. Never reach for a lighter grey to demote a label.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Measurement Rule
rules.body: Monospace is confined to measurement and data — counter, locators, level value, field values, grids, log, canvas tick labels. Names, labels and prose stay in the UI font.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Anything that changes while playing carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Well Earns Its Height Rule
rules.body: The tape well takes the pane's spare height (clamp(160px, 52vh, 520px)) only when there is a stream on it; on empty and error it collapses to 144px, because a full-height empty recess reads as a broken render.

rules.name: The Recess-Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows are always inset and always paired with a scored border. If a surface needs to read as separate, cut it in — never lift it out.

rules.name: The Scored Division Rule
rules.body: Regions are divided by 1px scored lines running edge to edge, never by gaps between rounded boxes and never by a filled band.

rules.name: The Two-Pixel Rule
rules.body: Every corner on the surface is 2px. A radius above 2px, or any fully rounded end, does not belong to this world.

dos: Do resolve every colour from a --vscode-* token, and derive any tone with color-mix against --cp-fg so it survives light themes.
Do divide regions with 1px scored hairlines that run edge to edge.
Do cut surfaces in with a scored border plus an inset shadow (the Recess-Only Rule).
Do use 2px corners on everything, and keep squares square.
Do carry label/value hierarchy as a size and form step — 10px tracked caps against 11.5px tabular mono (the Size-Step Rule).
Do put every measurement in the host's editor font with tabular-nums.
Do light exactly one key per action, using the foreground as the lamp, and add a non-colour cue (the label underline) alongside it.
Do spend the accent only on the stream — playhead, chunk register, and the swatch that keys it.
Do give a signal hue its -text variant whenever it is read as text.
Do branch high contrast explicitly: scores become contrastBorder, tints collapse, lit keys invert.
Do key responsive behaviour to container queries at 720px and 520px, and shrink the counter before removing anything.
Do state failure once, in the status band, with its recovery keys.
donts: Don't introduce an owned accent, a fixed hex palette, or an external font — the CSP forbids the font and the brief forbids the palette. Hex belongs only in a var() fallback.
Don't tint the ground behind small text, and don't use editorWidget-background as the plate.
Don't demote a label with a lighter tone; there is one ink.
Don't use descriptionForeground or any theme "muted" token for a label on this plate — measured at 3.4:1 (Dracula) and 3.6:1 (Solarized Light) against this ground.
Don't build depth with a drop shadow, a gradient, or imitation metal. Every shadow is inset.
Don't ship a pill, a capsule, a circle, or a radius above 2px — including a circular play button.
Don't separate rows with gaps between rounded boxes, or wrap a region in a filled card.
Don't stack an engraved caps label above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow. Engraved caps are field labels sat inline beside the value they name.
Don't stand a glyph, emoji, or icon-font character in for an icon: icons are authored inline SVG at 1.6 stroke weight with square caps, transport marks as solid geometry.
Don't animate anything that changes every frame — the millisecond register stays still — and don't add a motion that survives prefers-reduced-motion.
Don't let a second surface repeat a state the status band already owns, or leave a recess unlabelled when it is empty.
Don't reserve blank space for a control that has nothing to show; remove it.
